# What this program is about {.unnumbered}

This book documents a research program on **surrogates for steady, homogeneous,
boundary-driven PDEs**, developed around the `MeshTransformer` /
`MeshAttention` stack in `physicsnemo/experimental/nn/mesh_attention/` and the
exact/manufactured-label and solver-verified benchmark suite in
`examples/cfd/mesh_transformer/`.

The audience is applied mathematicians and ML researchers. The style is
first-principles: every architectural decision is stated as a hypothesis, and
the chapters record which hypotheses were supported or refuted.

::: {.callout-important title="Start with the program review"}
The authoritative, current synthesis of this program is
@sec-program-review-2026-08 — one chapter holding the frozen-instrument
frontier table, the five campaign verdicts, and their scope. The
short version: the program's product is `MeshTransformer2` (MT2), an
SE(3)-equivariant soft-slice transformer that is at in-family parity
with GeoTransolver on HiLiftAeroML (MT2/GT = 0.98) and 1.085× behind on
DrivAerML at best-vs-best learning rates; it is markedly more
learning-rate robust (1.55× degradation across a decade where
GeoTransolver loses 4--14×), the most density-robust architecture
measured once its similarity gauge is on (1.20× under 10:1 sampling bias
vs GeoTransolver's 3.6×), and about twice as expensive in training memory
(9.8 GB vs 4.6 GB). Its exact rotation equivariance is a contract, not an
accuracy edge: canonically trained GeoTransolver is exactly pose-invariant
at 1.01× cost on these datasets. Cross-family transfer turned out to be a
property of training-data diversity, not of any architecture tested;
query-independence is measured to trade 2.7--3.1× against accuracy and is
shelved with its price tag attached. An independent critic review on
2026-09-02 (`results/critic_review_2026-09-02.md`, @sec-nb-critic-review)
found that earlier versions of this book claimed contracts MT2 did not
have — similarity (scale) equivariance, measure completeness, equal cost,
a 1.6× equivariance dividend, and a label-noise explanation of the
DrivAerML gap; @sec-review-reframing records each retirement and the
measurement that replaced it. The live status of every experiment is the
tech tree of @sec-tech-tree. Everything below and in earlier chapters is
the historical evidence behind those sentences; the dated lab notebook
(@sec-notebook) holds every preregistration and verdict, including the
failed ones.
:::

## The thesis, in one paragraph

> The `MeshTransformer` treats physical structure as a set of **declared,
> per-problem contracts**, enforced by construction rather than learned:
> similarity equivariance always, with the scale gauge derived
> intrinsically from the geometry; drive-linearity when the problem is
> linear; parity typing when quantities are handed; drive-degree when the
> nonlinearity's order is known. Everything unknown — the PDE
> itself — is carried by operator-conditioned coefficients on a
> two-member exact singular dictionary. Each contract was earned by a
> falsification ladder recorded in this book, and several of those
> ladders fired against our own designs before they settled. The
> reference configuration is one attention layer, one full-width head,
> and two exact kernel members — roughly 82k parameters; its $\sim$104k
> benchmark-frozen sibling, kept fixed for comparability with every
> archived arm, outperforms a 27$\times$-larger physics-agnostic
> baseline in every regime tested
> (@sec-architecture states the design; @sec-benchmarks holds the
> evidence; @sec-notebook holds the history).

One scope line the industrial campaign added (2026-07-18): the
paragraph above is the *synthetic-program* thesis for the original
`MeshTransformer` (MT1), and there it is best supported within the
tested controlled suites. It does **not** describe the current product.
`MeshTransformer2` keeps exact rotation and translation covariance and
drops everything else in that paragraph — the kernel dictionary, the
superposition contract, query independence, and (until the 2026-09-03
similarity gauge, @sec-nb-s1-verdict) the intrinsic scale gauge itself;
@sec-mt2-architecture states what MT2 is. At industrial scale
the causal picture measured differently —
the completed attribution factorials showed the DrivAerML gains are
DOMINATED by the trace formulation — measured 3.8× at flagship
capacity, its two sub-mechanisms (exact jump correction, learned
own-cell readouts) near-perfect substitutes for the essential
boundary self-identification signal
(@sec-drivaerml-trace-factorial) — with capacity second and the
exact singular dictionary itself contributing 0–8% (its remaining
advantage is parameter efficiency: two zero-parameter closed-form
members match eight learned ones, @sec-drivaerml-factorial). The
industrial model is accurately described as boundary-integral-inspired;
its strongest measured industrial asset is out-of-distribution
behavior (@sec-drivaerml), where the deep-S1 wall-shear-direction
degradation-ratio differential against the strongest baseline is
consistent at five seeds per side but remains provisional: the paired
sample is too small for a two-sided 5% exact sign decision, the metric
record is contradictory, and the baseline's absolute WSS error is
still 2.5–2.7× lower. The pressure differential is suggestive only
(@sec-program-review).

A second scope line, corrected by the 2026-07-27 audit: the
out-of-distribution asset is measured **within** the DrivAer family.
Pushed to a different vehicle family, zero-shot, every tested
checkpoint diverged while a gauge-agnostic baseline stayed structured
(@sec-drivaerml-crossfamily). The exploratory gauge dose-response did
not identify the cause: intrinsic-gauge retraining also failed, and
the supposedly train-only calibration included held-out cases. More
decisively, offset-free diagnostics show that every tested field
pattern is essentially unrelated to truth. The supported industrial
generalization claim is therefore within-family and provisional
(@sec-program-review).

## Problem statement and scope

The object to learn is a single mapping:

$$
\{\text{boundary geometry},\ \text{BC types},\ \text{BC values}\}
\;\longmapsto\;
\text{interior field at specified query points}.
$$

This is not a time update. In contrast to most neural-PDE work there is no
volume state to advance: no volume mesh, no time stepping, and no data of
any kind attached to the interior query points — they are bare coordinates
at which the steady field is requested.

The admitted problem class is **well-posed** (in the Hadamard sense),
**homogeneous** steady PDEs — no position-dependent interior source terms —
governed by the **same equations everywhere** in the domain (no piecewise
materials; those are future coupled subproblems). The eventual targets are
steady RANS and steady Euler.

Critically, **the governing equations are not given.** For the real targets
they are not even perfectly knowable: turbulence closures are empirical
curve fits, not derived operators. Exact fundamental solutions are therefore
unavailable *by problem statement* — a learned kernel family may be *biased
toward* typical-PDE behavior (a singularity dictionary as an inductive
prior), but no rigorous PDE specialization can be assumed in deployment.

What the problem class *does* license is one strong structural assumption:
because the equations are homogeneous and identical everywhere in the
domain, the boundary-to-interior propagation law is **equivariant under the
similarity group** — translations, rotations/reflections, and positive
scalings. Translations force kernels of the relative displacement $x - y$;
rotational symmetry is broken *only* by directional data on the boundary
(the normal $n_y$, and the direction of any vector-valued boundary values).
Kernels therefore depend on the geometry through **joint invariants of
$\{x - y,\ n_y,\ \text{boundary vector data}\}$** — never through absolute
position or absolute orientation. Boundary *scalar* data (Dirichlet traces,
flux magnitudes, global parameters like the nondimensional screening
constant $\tilde\kappa = \kappa R$) enters the kernels
freely: scalars are directionless, so they can modulate everything without
ever breaking rotational symmetry. The domain dependence lives in the
boundary solve, not in the kernel (@sec-pde-theory).

The benchmarks in this book pose the simplest members of the
class — problems like

$$
\Delta u = 0 \ \text{ in } \Omega,
\qquad u = g \ \text{ on } \partial\Omega,
$$

whose answers *are* known — because exact labels and exact fundamental
solutions make every structural claim falsifiable. Keeping the two settings
distinct is the job of this section: the *benchmarks* know the PDE; the
*product* does not.

The goal is *not* only in-distribution accuracy. A learned operator is only
useful if it behaves like an operator, which the program measures along four
independent out-of-distribution axes:

1. **geometry** — unseen shape modes, stronger deformations, new topology;
2. **boundary data** — the boundary values driving the solution (the
   "drive"): frequencies never seen in training;
3. **PDE parameters** — e.g. the screening constant of $\Delta u - \kappa^2 u = 0$;
4. **resolution** — boundary discretizations finer or coarser than training.

## Design constraints

Every model in the program must satisfy, *by construction rather than by
augmentation*:

- **Equivariance / similarity covariance.** Translation invariance,
  O($D$) covariance for scalars and polar vectors, and positive-scale
  covariance when the declared reference length transforms with the geometry.
- **Dimensional consistency.** All fields enter nondimensionalized; the
  reference length rescales only coordinates and measures. What is banned
  is any length that fails to transform covariantly — fitted constants,
  training-set statistics; a per-instance, similarity-covariant functional
  of the input geometry (the radius-of-gyration gauge of
  @sec-forward-pass) is licensed precisely because it transforms with the
  data. MT2 violated this constraint for a month without anyone
  noticing — its reference length was a constant pinned in a config
  file — until the critic review of 2026-09-02 (@sec-nb-critic-review);
  the `similarity_gauge` repair of @sec-nb-s1-verdict restores it.
- **All-to-all information flow.** Elliptic solutions couple every boundary
  point to every interior point (@sec-global-flow); graph neighborhoods,
  distance cutoffs, and locality heuristics are excluded.
- **Zero-drive preservation always; exact linearity when the problem is
  linear.** A homogeneous problem with zero boundary data has the zero
  solution — structural in every field mode. Superposition is an additional
  per-problem contract, enforced to floating point when (and only when) the
  governing PDE is declared linear; it is never an assumption of the
  architecture.
- **Exact query-point independence.** The prediction at $x$ must not depend on
  which other query points are requested.

## The headline

The comparison below spans two fundamentally different *model classes*, and it
is important to read it that way:

- **General-purpose architectures** (red/orange) know nothing about Laplace's
  equation. `MeshTransformer` accepts arbitrary named boundary-condition
  schemas, scalar and vector fields, and global parameters; the free-form
  pair kernel is an unconstrained MLP of pair invariants. Their capacity is
  spent *learning* what the PDE does. The purple circle — `MeshTransformer`
  with the kernel-basis query decoder that repairs qualification 2 below, in
  its dictionary-only variant (@sec-kernel-decoder) — is this same
  architecture class with one explicit asterisk: its kernel
  dictionary contains one Laplace-family member (the exact double-layer
  singular kernel) alongside PDE-agnostic polynomial members, which is why
  it wears its own color.
- **PDE-conforming learned BIE models** (green/blue) know the PDE family and
  learn only *which member* of the analytic layer-potential family solves the
  problem. The pruned **"3-parameter BIE"** (`HarmonicPanelBIE`) is exactly
  this: its three scalars are (i) $c_1$, a learned multiple of the Laplace
  double-layer kernel, integrated *exactly* over boundary panels; (ii)
  $\alpha$, the relaxation of an unrolled eight-step second-kind boundary
  solve; and (iii) $d_0$, a constant-kernel coefficient that trains to
  $\approx 0$. Nothing else. It is a boundary-element method whose kernel
  coefficient and solver relaxation are the only things learned.

The benchmark is *exactly* Laplace — favorable to the specialist by
construction. The PDE-conforming results are
**oracle-in-family diagnostics**: on a problem whose answer is known, they
quantify the value of each structural ingredient (factorization, kernel
basis, singular quadrature, learned solve) and characterize what a learned
kernel family must look like to behave as an operator. They are *not* the
product design — under the scope above, the deployed model cannot assume a
known kernel.

```{python}
#| fig-cap: >
#|   Parameter count versus in-distribution relative L2 error on the frozen
#|   64-case reference bank (identical evaluation protocol for every model;
#|   data from the checked-in results/learned_bie_2026-07-02.json).
#|   Circles: general-purpose, PDE-agnostic architectures. Squares:
#|   Laplace-specific learned boundary-integral models. The purple circle is
#|   the kernel-decoder repair (dictionary-only variant): general-purpose
#|   architecture whose kernel dictionary contains one Laplace-family member
#|   (the exact double-layer singular kernel) -- hence its own color. The
#|   Every row uses 3,000 training updates and 3 seeds on this bank,
#|   except the 13-parameter model, whose only reference-bank protocol is
#|   1,000 updates (its 3,000-update values exist only on the early
#|   bank).
import json
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

results = json.load(open(Path("..") / "results" / "learned_bie_2026-07-02.json"))
comparisons = results["comparisons_same_bank"]
confirmation = results["iteration_4_pruning"]["confirmation_3seed_reference_bank"]
refbank = results["iteration_7_kernel_decoder_fix"][
    "reference_bank_3seed_3000steps"]
kernel_dict = refbank["kernel_dictionary_only"]


def mean(values):
    return sum(values) / len(values)


models = [
    ("MeshTransformer\n(moment decoder)",
     comparisons["mesh_transformer_reference"]["parameters"],
     mean(refbank["moment_decoder"]["id"]), "#e34948", "o",
     "general-purpose (PDE-agnostic)"),
    ("free-form invariant\npair kernel",
     comparisons["invariant_pair_kernel"]["parameters"],
     mean(refbank["pair_kernel_control"]["id"]), "#eda100", "o",
     "general-purpose (PDE-agnostic)"),
    ("MeshTransformer\n(kernel decoder, dictionary-only)",
     kernel_dict["parameters"],
     sum(kernel_dict["id"]) / len(kernel_dict["id"]), "#8352c9", "o",
     "general-purpose + one Laplace-family\ndictionary member"),
    ("harmonic-panel BIE (13 p)", 13,
     results["results_3seed_reference_bank"]["interpolation_relative_l2"]["mean"],
     "#1baf7a", "s", "PDE-conforming learned BIE"),
    ("harmonic-panel BIE,\npruned (3 p)", 3,
     confirmation["interpolation"]["mean"], "#2a78d6", "s",
     "PDE-conforming learned BIE"),
]

label_style = {
    "harmonic-panel BIE,\npruned (3 p)": dict(xytext=(10, -4), ha="left"),
    "free-form invariant\npair kernel": dict(xytext=(-10, 2), ha="right"),
    "MeshTransformer\n(kernel decoder, dictionary-only)":
        dict(xytext=(10, -14), ha="left"),
}

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.4, 3.9))
seen = set()
for label, params, err, color, marker, cls in models:
    ax.plot(params, err, marker, ms=9, color=color, zorder=3,
            label=cls if cls not in seen else None)
    seen.add(cls)
    style = label_style.get(label, dict(xytext=(8, 2), ha="left"))
    ax.annotate(label, (params, err), textcoords="offset points",
                fontsize=8.5, color="#52514e", **style)
ax.set_xscale("log")
ax.set_yscale("log")
ax.set_xlim(1, 3e6)
ax.set_xlabel("trainable parameters")
ax.set_ylabel("ID relative $L^2$ (64-case bank)")
ax.grid(True, color="#e1e0d9", lw=0.8)
ax.legend(loc="upper left", fontsize=8.5, frameon=False)
for spine in ("top", "right"):
    ax.spines[spine].set_visible(False)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

(The kernel-decoder repair of qualification 2 below is plotted from its
three-seed reference-bank rows — same frozen 64-case bank, 3,000 updates —
so the figure mixes no banks. The plotted variant is *dictionary-only*: at
3,000 updates the full dictionary's near-zero-initialized smooth MLP
members grow to absorb ID error at the expense of frequency-OOD (0.12
$\to$ 0.49), and ablating them restores freq-OOD 0.0713 at identical ID —
the dictionary-selection finding of @sec-kernel-decoder.^[Why the purple
point wears its own color: the architecture is fully general-purpose —
arbitrary BC schemas, fields, global parameters — but its kernel
dictionary contains one Laplace-family member, the exact double-layer
singular kernel, so it is not as PDE-agnostic as the red/orange class on
this benchmark.])

::: {.callout-note title="How to read this figure"}
This is **not** a like-for-like architecture ranking, and it does not say
"attention is worse." It says that on a fixed, known, homogeneous linear PDE
— the benchmark setting, not the product setting — encoding the PDE's
fundamental-solution structure in the decoder lets a 3-parameter model
match the strongest generic control in-distribution at matched budget
(0.035 vs 0.040) with over four orders of magnitude fewer parameters —
and beat it 7–10$\times$ on frequency-OOD (0.066 vs 0.50–0.64, matched
and 1,000-update protocols respectively). Three qualifications matter:

1. The specialist is the measuring instrument, not the goal. It cannot leave
   its PDE family, and under the program's scope the deployed model must:
   the target problems' equations are not given. The generalist path —
   unknown operators, nonlinear closures, learned conditioning (where, in
   the parametric study of @sec-parametric, conditioned models beat the pure
   basis *in distribution* by a factor of six) — is the actual product goal;
   the specialist rows calibrate how much each piece of structure is worth.
2. The `MeshTransformer` point sits high partly because of a *diagnosed*
   defect — the proved $m \le 2$ angular ceiling of its moment decoder
   (@sec-mesh-attention) — not because attention over boundaries is
   inherently limited. The direct repair is confirmed — three seeds, 3,000
   updates, on this figure's reference bank: a kernel-basis query decoder
   (`query_decoder="kernel"`) removes the ceiling and cuts ID error
   11.3$\times$ (0.4503 $\to$ 0.0399); its dictionary-only variant is the
   purple circle above (ID 0.0409, freq-OOD 0.0713) (@sec-kernel-decoder).
3. All models satisfy the same exact contracts (equivariance, superposition,
   query independence); the comparison isolates representation, not
   constraint discipline.
:::

The pruned model reaches ID relative $L^2$ of $0.0347\pm0.0006$ on the
reference bank, with frequency-OOD error $0.0664\pm0.0004$, and its kernel
coefficient converges to the analytic double-layer constant $-1/2\pi$ within
$0.8\%$ on every seed. On the easier early evaluation bank (seed 17, same
3,000-step budget) it approaches the analytic oracle itself (ID $0.0056$ vs
oracle $0.003$). The same recipe transfers to Neumann data (ID $0.0029$ at
10,000 steps) and, with the screening parameter placed in the kernel basis,
to the screened Laplace family.

The interesting part is not the small model per se — it is the
**falsification ladder** that isolated *why* it works (@sec-ladder). Each of
the three ingredients was refuted individually:

| Ingredient removed | What happens |
|---|---|
| learned solve without a PDE-conforming kernel | frequency-OOD *worsens* (0.61 → 0.76) |
| harmonicity as a soft penalty instead of exact structure | residual halves; frequency-OOD *worsens* (0.61 $\to$ 0.71) |
| exact harmonic kernel without singular quadrature | loses even to the free-form MLP (ID 0.65) |

: The three single-ingredient refutations (seed 17, early bank; details in @sec-ladder). {#tbl-refutations}

shows breadth: every benchmark suite in the program, with the
parameter-free floor, the best `MeshTransformer` arm, the strongest
comparator run on that suite, and the oracle where one exists.

```{python}

    ("deep cavity", None, 0.067, 0.115, False, None),
    # it23 singpair_pseudo ID (5 seeds); it22 trace-informed control
    ("potential flow", None, 0.028, 0.178, False, None),
    # it25 floor arm; nl_pseudo combined ID (5 seeds)
    ("Euler–Bernoulli", 1.0, 0.046, None, None, None),
    # it33 floor arm; it35 q2 combined ID (3 seeds)
    ("rotational Euler", 0.944, 0.072, None, None, None),
    # it36 boundary_mean eval_id combined; nl_pseudo eval_id combined;

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.2, 4.2))
x = range(len(suites))
series = [
    (1, None, "parameter-free floor",

    (3, True, "Transolver (steel-manned)",
     dict(marker="o", ms=7, color="#e34948", mec="white", mew=1.0)),
```

## Research tech tree {#sec-tech-tree}

The generalization campaign — the program's current phase — is run as an
explicit tech tree: every experiment is a node with a preregistered
question, a dependency, an acceptance criterion, and a dated verdict in
the lab notebook (@sec-notebook). Three architectures recur throughout.
**MeshTransformer2 (MT2)** is the program's product: an SE(3)-equivariant
slice-routing surrogate — exact under rotations and translations by
construction, with a measure-weighted similarity gauge (measure-weighted
centroid and RMS-radius reference length) as the reference configuration
for new runs since 2026-09-03; the checkpoints most of this book reports
predate that gauge and saw absolute scale through a constant reference
length (@sec-mt2-architecture). **GeoTransolver** is the strongest
external baseline, a soft-slice global-attention architecture with
pointwise raw-coordinate features and no equivariance contract.
**MeshTransformer (MT1)** is the original GLOBE-lineage architecture,
retained where its drive-linearity contract and exact kernel decoder make
it the exactness reference. The central open question the tree is
organized around is the **G2 transfer gap**: on the frozen
DrivAerML→SHIFT-SUV instrument, GeoTransolver's zero-shot error on a
held-out vehicle family improves with in-family training data (0.784 →
0.657 across five rungs, two seeds per rung, with per-seed reversals
inside the spread) while MT2's stays flat — the one measured axis where
the baseline generalizes and the structured model does not.

The refutation wave of 2026-08-20/21 resolved every mechanism candidate
then on the table, and the instrument wave and critic review of
2026-09-01/03 then re-examined the premises. Two of the wave's closures
did not survive: M1 tested a scale symmetry MT2 never had (its reference
length was a constant), and M4 declared measure-complete a model whose
centroid was an unweighted mean; S1 repaired both and measured the
effect. With MT2 genuinely similarity-covariant, its zero-shot transfer
did not move, so absolute size is ruled out as the G2 carrier
(@sec-nb-s1-verdict). What remains as the candidate explanation of the
G2 transfer gap is GeoTransolver's **pointwise raw coordinate features**
and its **non-equivariant global encoder**. The discriminating experiment
in flight is the HiLift generalization ladder (HLGEN). The exact-kernel
line that G3K revived generalizes across boundary-condition frequency
content on 2D Laplace, but the K0 gate showed that inviscid potential
flow is not a usable prior for separated bluff-body aerodynamics, so it
does not launch on DrivAerML.

: The tech-tree ledger. Every status is as of 2026-09-03; evidence links go to the dated lab-notebook entry holding the preregistration and verdict. Rows whose verdicts were later voided, retracted, or overturned say so and link both the original and the correcting entry. {#tbl-tech-tree}

## How the book is organized

- @sec-pde-theory develops the PDE background: Green representation, boundary
  integral equations, the second-kind Fredholm structure, and the similarity
  group — the theory every design decision traces back to — and closes by
  separating what is PDE-agnostic (assumable under the product scope) from
  what is specific to a known fundamental solution.
- @sec-architecture is the plain-language source of truth for what the
  `MeshTransformer` *is*: inputs, outputs, the forward pass, the typed
  scalar/vector channels, and the reference configuration that current
  evidence selects.
- @sec-mesh-attention is the mathematics behind that description — the
  exact layer forms, the contracts, the proved angular ceiling, and the
  kernel-basis query decoder that removes it. The stack is a
  transformer-native generalization of GLOBE (arXiv
  [2511.15856](https://arxiv.org/abs/2511.15856)).
- @sec-learned-bie walks the falsification ladder to the learned
  boundary-integral model, including the Neumann extension and the pruning
  study.
- @sec-parametric asks where a global PDE parameter should enter a learned
  surrogate — basis or conditioning — and answers it experimentally.
- @sec-benchmarks is the results reference, organized by message in six
  parts: how we evaluate; the declared contracts and their walls; what
  carries the accuracy; generalization stress-tests; the Transolver
  steel-man; and solver-labeled viscous flow.
- @sec-future reviews where the program stands, lays out the redirected
  agenda, and keeps a candid engineering review.
- @sec-notebook is the lab notebook: the dated, iteration-by-iteration
  record of hypotheses, refutations, and course corrections behind every
  claim in the clean chapters.

## Provenance and caveats

All quantitative claims come from two kinds of artifacts, and the text marks
which is which:

- **Checked-in results** under `examples/cfd/mesh_transformer/results/`
  (`reference_2026-07-01.json`, `architectural_ablation_2026-07-01.json`,
  `learned_bie_2026-07-02.json`) — frozen banks, fixed seeds, recorded
  protocols.
- **Session artifacts** under `/tmp` on the original machine (training
  histories, checkpoints). Figures built from these are labeled; they have not
  been reproduced elsewhere.

Standing caveats, stated once here: the benchmark evidence is 2D and 3D
on exact-label suites (Laplace, screened Laplace, Liouville, potential
flow, Euler–Bernoulli, rotational Euler) plus two FEM-labeled dataset
suites — the linear Laplace catalog and the iteration-36 steady
Navier–Stokes suite (@sec-ns-cavity), whose label-noise floor is
measured and reported; solver-labeled RANS remains the next ledge;
several early
ablations are seed-17-only where noted; the early external baselines
(GLOBE, and radius-free GeoTransolver — an in-tree geometry-conditioned
Transolver variant) were limited to 1,000-update controls and have since
been superseded as evidence by the steel-manned Transolver
comparison in both training regimes; and the complete, current caveat
ledger is the standing-caveats section of @sec-future, which is kept
up to date as results become available.
